1.text: A fresh breeze blew through the open window. Zech was busy cutting cardstock to make a giant green pinwheel. Chike brought over a tiny LED light bulb with two wires. "Can your paper pinwheel turn on this light without a battery?" Chike asked. "Watch this!" Zech replied.

2.text: Stacey blew air through a bamboo tube at the pinwheel. Fwip-fwip-fwip! The paper blades spun fast, and the workshop transformed into a breezy, green hill. Giant white wind turbines towered above them against a blue sky!

4.text: "Wind has kinetic energy: energy from movement," Zech explained. He curved the paper blades so they could catch even the softest breeze. As the wind pushed the curved blades, a tiny generator inside spun around, making real electricity!

6.text: Chike connected the wires, and a miniature paper house lit up! Whoosh! The windy hill faded back into the workshop. The tiny LED light bulb was still glowing brightly on Zech's desk. "Nature gives us power everywhere," Zech said. "We just have to catch it!"

8.text: What Zech learned “The wind was there all along,” Zech said. “I just had to build something that could catch it.”
